531.text: The end of the peach branch

215.text: his visitor , whom he took for a prospector like himself

539.text: this gray - faced , thoughtful old prospector

569.text: a small , forked branch of a peach tree

quotes.text: "I saw your fire.  May I make camp here?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"We might stay together, if it's
all right with you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It's a big place.
If we find gold there'll be enough for two."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't go down into the desert for gold alone,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I
may strike through the Sonora Desert.  I may head for Pinacate or north
for the Colorado Basin.  You are an old man."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't know the country, but to me one place is the same as another,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Yes, I'm old.  I'm lonely, too.  It's come to me just lately.  But,
friend, I can still travel, and for a few days my company won't hurt
you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Get the little basket in my pack,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown
